artiest/krontjong-toegoe.text:
Krontjong Toegoe is a kroncong ensemble from Tugu, an old district in the north of Jakarta. The name belongs to a community with a long history. In 1661 the Dutch East India Company freed Portuguese prisoners and slaves from Goa in Kampung Tugu, on condition that they convert from Catholicism to Protestantism. Their descendants preserved the music that the Portuguese sailors had brought with them.

That music is called kroncong. The name probably comes from the jangling sound of the accompaniment. A kroncong orchestra usually consists of two ukulele-like small guitars, a cello, a guitar and a bass. The ukuleles play interlocking rhythms, somewhat as in a gamelan, while the singing or melody moves more calmly above them. In this way an Indonesian musical tradition arose on European instruments.

The melancholy mood of unamplified kroncong resembles that of Portuguese fado. The Tugu ensemble has kept the tradition alive and has performed, among other places, at the Pasar Malam Besar in The Hague, a well-known festival of the Indo-Dutch community. Many young Indonesians now regard kroncong as old-fashioned folk music, but since 2016 the genre has been recognised as part of Indonesia's national intangible cultural heritage. The ensemble shows how Portuguese, Dutch and Indonesian influences come together in a single sound.
artiest/krontjong-toegoe.listen: Listen to Kr. Padang Bulan and notice the fast, rhythmic accompaniment of the small stringed instruments beneath the calmer melody. Try to hear which instruments carry the rhythm.

artiest/kruder-en-dorfmeister.text:
Kruder & Dorfmeister is an Austrian duo from Vienna, named after its two members, Peter Kruder, born in 1967, and Richard Dorfmeister, born in 1968. They are known for their trip hop and downtempo remixes of pop songs, hip hop and drum 'n' bass. Their first EP, G-Stoned, appeared in 1993, featuring the hypnotic High Noon. The sleeve resembled that of Bookends by Simon & Garfunkel. The record received glowing reviews, particularly in Britain, and Gilles Peterson was the first to play the track on his BBC programme Worldwide.

The duo made their name with remixes for artists including Roni Size, William Orbit, Lamb, Madonna and Depeche Mode. This earned them a strong reputation, even though they had hardly any album of their own. DJ-Kicks: Kruder & Dorfmeister appeared in 1996 and The K & D Sessions, the record that contains their best-known remixes, in 1998. Alongside the duo, Kruder released a solo record in 2001 as Peace Orchestra, and Dorfmeister made records such as Opera and Suzuki under the name Tosca. Their own label, G-Stone Recordings, became a home for this Viennese scene.

The music is slow, soft and warm: relaxed breaks, deep basses and plenty of space between the sounds. In this way Vienna was put on the map of electronic music. In 2010 they celebrated sixteen years of G-Stone with a compilation and a world tour with the show K&D Sessions Live.
artiest/kruder-en-dorfmeister.listen: Listen to High Noon and notice the slow tempo, the spacious bass and how a simple rhythmic line can keep running for a long time without becoming boring.

artiest/krystian-zimerman.text:
Krystian Zimerman is a Polish pianist, conductor and teacher, born in Zabrze in 1956. He began playing the piano at the age of five, encouraged by his father, who was also a pianist. He studied in Katowice with Andrzej Jasiński and in 1975 won the International Chopin Piano Competition in Warsaw. That was the beginning of his international career. In 1976 he played with the Berlin Philharmonic, and in 1979 he made his United States debut with the New York Philharmonic. Arthur Rubinstein invited him to Paris, and their friendship lasted until Rubinstein's death in 1982.

Zimerman worked with conductors such as Leonard Bernstein, Herbert von Karajan, Pierre Boulez, Carlo Maria Giulini and Simon Rattle. His well-known recordings include the piano concertos by Grieg and Schumann with Karajan, the Brahms concertos with Bernstein, the Chopin concertos and solo works by Chopin, Liszt, Debussy and Schubert. Witold Lutosławski wrote his Piano Concerto for him. He is best known for his interpretations of Romantic music, but he also plays other repertoire and supports contemporary music.

Since 1996 he has taught at the music academy in Basel, and in 1999 he founded the Polish Festival Orchestra, to mark the 150th anniversary of Chopin's death. Zimerman is regarded as one of the greatest pianists of his generation. His Chopin playing was and is seen as a point of reference: precise, clear and never merely beautiful for its own sake.
artiest/krystian-zimerman.listen: Listen to one of Chopin's Ballades in his recording and notice how he almost whispers the soft passages while keeping the loud sections clear.

artiest/krzysztof-komeda.text: Krzysztof Komeda's real name was Krzysztof Trzciński, and he was born in Poznań in 1931. He trained as an ear, nose and throat doctor and used his stage name to keep his jazz work separate from his job. In 1956 his sextet played at the first jazz festival in Sopot. Komeda sought a European jazz with Slavic melodies, slow tempos and plenty of space. His album Astigmatic (1965), with Tomasz Stańko and Zbigniew Namysłowski, is regarded as the high point of Polish jazz. He wrote the music for films by Roman Polański, such as Nóż w wodzie (Knife in the Water) (1962) and Rosemary's Baby (1968). After a fall in Los Angeles he fell into a coma; he died in Warsaw in 1969.
artiest/krzysztof-komeda.listen: Listen to the slow, sombre melody and the space between the notes.

artiest/krzysztof-penderecki.text:
Krzysztof Penderecki was a Polish composer and conductor, born in Dębica in 1933 and died in 2020. He studied violin and then composition at the music academy in Kraków, where he also began teaching after graduating in 1958. In 1959 he first attracted international attention at the Warsaw Autumn festival. His breakthrough came with Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima, a piece for string orchestra from 1960.

In his early work Penderecki used the orchestra as a source of sound. Strings play dense tone clusters, glissandi and unconventional playing techniques, and in other pieces even typewriters and gongs can be heard. His notation abandoned the ordinary stave and drew sounds that change. At the same time he wrote religious music, such as the St Luke Passion of 1963 to 1966, which combines avant-garde language with Baroque forms. Such works came into being in communist Eastern Europe.

In the mid-1970s, when he was a professor at Yale, he chose a more traditional and tonal sound. His Polish Requiem grew out of a piece for Solidarity in Gdańsk. Penderecki also wrote music for film and theatre. His work showed that an orchestra could produce new and unsettling sounds.
artiest/krzysztof-penderecki.listen: Listen to Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima and notice how the strings produce mainly sound rather than melody. Can you hear the dense clouds of sound, the glissandi and the high, piercing notes?

artiest/kudsi-erguner.text: Kudsi Erguner, born in Diyarbakır, learned the ney, the reed flute of the Mevlevi dervishes, from his father Ulvi Erguner. In the 1970s he moved to Paris, where in the early 1980s he founded an institute for Sufi music. He recorded old Ottoman repertoires and also played with jazz musicians, with Peter Gabriel and with the oud player Anouar Brahem. On Sufi Music of Turkey (1990) he plays the music of the whirling dervishes with his brother Süleyman.
artiest/kudsi-erguner.listen: Listen to the ney in Tales from the Ney: the note begins with audible breath and then swells, as if the flute itself were sighing.

artiest/kudsi-erguner-en-suleyman-ergune.text:
Kudsi Ergüner is a Turkish musician, born in Diyarbakır in 1952. He is regarded as a master of the traditional Sufi music of the Mevlevi and as one of the best-known players of the ney, the Turkish flute. As a child he learned from his father Ulvi Ergüner and attended the sema, the Mevlevi ceremony, and other dervish rituals. In 1969 he began his career at the radio in Istanbul.

In the 1970s Kudsi Ergüner moved to Paris. In the early 1980s he founded the Mevlana Institute there, for research into and teaching of classical Sufi music. With his own ensemble he played both improvised forms from the classical Ottoman tradition and pieces dating back to the thirteenth century. For decades he searched for the oldest roots of Ottoman music, which he also taught and recorded.

He also collaborated with Western musicians. He played on Peter Gabriel's soundtrack for The Last Temptation of Christ and worked with the director Peter Brook and the choreographer Maurice Béjart. In 2016 he became a UNESCO Artist for Peace. His work connects a spiritual tradition of centuries with the contemporary concert stage.
artiest/kudsi-erguner-en-suleyman-ergune.listen: Listen to Zikr and notice the breathy sound of the ney, with its soft, almost spoken tone. Try to hear how the flute and the other instruments together create a meditative atmosphere.

artiest/kuk-harrell.text:
Kuk Harrell, whose full name is Thaddis Laphonia Harrell, is an American songwriter, arranger, sound engineer and vocal producer. He was born in 1964 and began his career in Chicago as a drummer and singer. He then worked as a session musician and wrote music for commercials for companies including McDonald's and Coca-Cola. In 1992 he moved to Los Angeles, where he sang on songs by Diane Warren and David Foster.

In 2004 he went to work in Atlanta at RedZone Entertainment, the production company of his cousins Tricky Stewart and Mark Stewart. There he formed a team with Stewart and Terius Nash, better known as The-Dream. Harrell's speciality was vocals: as vocal producer he was responsible for how the voice sounded on the record. Mark Stewart called him the team's secret weapon. In 2007 he co-wrote Rihanna's Umbrella, with a rap by Jay-Z, and produced the vocals. The song won a Grammy. He also worked on Beyoncé's Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It), Mary J. Blige's Growing Pains and Justin Bieber's My World 2.0.

Harrell is an example of a profession that became increasingly important in the hit factory of the 2000s. A hit no longer arose from a song and a singer alone, but from a team in which someone concentrated entirely on how the voice sounds. His name is rarely printed large on the sleeve, but his work can be heard on many of the biggest hits of his time.
artiest/kuk-harrell.listen: Listen to Rihanna's Umbrella and notice the vocals in the chorus: the word umbrella is stretched out and repeated as ella, ella, eh, eh. Hear how Rihanna's voice is layered there and how that hook sticks in your head.

artiest/kulgrinda.text:
Kūlgrinda is a folk group from Vilnius in Lithuania, founded in 1989 by Jonas Trinkūnas and his wife Inija Trinkūnienė. They were leaders of Romuva, a contemporary movement that revives the ancient Baltic religion. From the start the group has been the musical voice of that movement and often plays at its ceremonies. Romuva's website describes it as a ritual folklore group. The name comes from a secret underwater road in Samogitia.

The music is simple and sounds as if it has had little studio processing. The emphasis is on the voices. The group has devoted itself to sutartinės, a traditional form of polyphonic singing in which several singers sing interlocking melodies. Through rhythmic repetition a pattern arises that one musicologist compares to the weaving of a multicoloured cloth. Albums such as Perkūno giesmės from 2003 and Laimos giesmės from 2014 contain ritual songs.

Kūlgrinda collaborated with the electronic musician Donis, the singer Rasa Serra and the metal band Ugnėlakis. The last of these collaborations gave rise to the folk rock group Žalvarinis. In this way the group is a bridge between age-old Lithuanian singing traditions and the modern folk scene.
artiest/kulgrinda.listen: Listen to Kada Buva Kadujo, Geri Metai Kadujo and notice how the voices become interwoven. Try to hear how repetition and rhythm form a pattern, without any one voice taking the lead.

artiest/kurt-cobain.text:
Kurt Cobain was the singer, guitarist and principal songwriter of Nirvana. He was born in 1967 in Aberdeen, a small port town in the American state of Washington. As a child he sang and drew a great deal. His parents' divorce, when he was nine, made him quiet and rebellious. Through Buzz Osborne of the Melvins he discovered punk and hardcore, and in the punk scene around Seattle he found his place. Later he named Pixies, The Vaselines and Meat Puppets as favourites.

In 1987 Cobain started a band with the bassist Krist Novoselic that was called Nirvana from 1988. The debut album Bleach appeared in 1989 on the small label Sub Pop. With the drummer Dave Grohl, who joined in 1990, the band signed to the major label DGC. The second album, Nevermind (1991), was a smash with Smells Like Teen Spirit. Cobain also wrote Come as You Are, Lithium, In Bloom and, for the last studio album In Utero (1993), Heart-Shaped Box and All Apologies. His music combined the noise of punk with melodies that stuck in the mind, and his lyrics were restless and full of doubt.

Because of the sudden success Cobain came to be seen as the voice of Generation X, a role in which he did not feel at home. He struggled with depression, stomach pain, a heroin addiction and the pressure of fame. In April 1994, at the age of 27, he took his own life. With his songs he widened what mainstream rock could be about, and he is regarded as one of the most influential rock musicians. In 2014 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Nirvana.
artiest/kurt-cobain.listen: Listen to Smells Like Teen Spirit by Nirvana. Notice how the quiet verses with thin guitar give way to the loud, distorted chorus.

artiest/kurt-weill.text:
Kurt Weill was born in Dessau in 1900, the son of a cantor in a Jewish congregation. He had piano lessons at the age of twelve, wrote songs at an early age and studied in Berlin with Engelbert Humperdinck and later with Ferruccio Busoni. In his view his music had to serve a socially useful purpose, which he called Gebrauchsmusik. The best-known example is his work with the writer Bertolt Brecht, and within that above all Die Dreigroschenoper, which contains the ballad Mack the Knife.

In 1933 Weill fled Nazi Germany. Two years later he arrived in the United States and settled in New York. There he wrote for Broadway, including Lady in the Dark, One Touch of Venus from 1943 and Street Scene from 1947. His song September Song became a standard. With Brecht he had also made Die sieben Todsünden, a ballet with singing. His wife, the singer Lotte Lenya, continued to perform his music, for example on Lotte Lenya singt Kurt Weill.

Weill also wrote for the concert hall and made works on Jewish themes. He died in 1950. His music is a bridge between classical composition, cabaret and jazz: sharp harmonies, dance rhythms and lyrics that are often socially engaged. Many jazz musicians later played his songs anew, and Mack the Knife became a worldwide hit.
artiest/kurt-weill.listen: Listen to Mack the Knife in a version from Die Dreigroschenoper and notice the simple, almost childlike melody and how it contrasts with the gruesome lyrics.

artiest/kyla.text:
Kyla, born Melanie Hernandez Calumpad in 1981, is a Filipino singer, actress and television personality. She began as a child with singing contests, won a talent competition at the age of twelve and at thirteen became a member of the variety show That's Entertainment. In 1997 she came third in Metropop Star Search. Only in 2000, after being turned down by several labels, did she get a contract with EMI Philippines, and her debut album Way to Your Heart was released.

The single Hanggang Ngayon won the MTV Video Music Award for Southeast Asia in 2001. It was followed by Kyla in 2002, on which she began writing herself and on which soul and R&B can be heard, I Will Be There in 2003 with the British boy band Blue, Not Your Ordinary Girl in 2004 and Beautiful Days in 2006. Later came the cover albums Heartfelt and Heart 2 Heart and, in 2010, Private Affair. Her ninth album appeared in 2018 after a new contract with Star Music. Her first seven records all went platinum.

Kyla is known for her range and her melismatic singing style, in which she stretches a syllable over several notes. In this way she has made R&B and soul popular in the Philippines, and the media call her the country's Queen of R&B. She has also worked as an actress in TV series, presented the talent show Popstar Kids and was a judge on Tawag ng Tanghalan.
artiest/kyla.listen: Listen to Hanggang Ngayon and notice how she changes pitch on some syllables, a hallmark of R&B that stands out strongly in her voice.

artiest/kyle-dixon.text:
Kyle Dixon is an American composer and electronic musician who has worked with Michael Stein for years. They began in the electronic scene of Austin, Texas, and in 2009, together with Adam Jones and Mark Donica, formed the synthesizer band Survive. Survive's music is associated with analogue synthesizers, playing live with equipment and the sounds of horror and science fiction films. Under the name Short Hour, Dixon and Stein also make music for film, television and installations.

Their big breakthrough came with the Netflix series Stranger Things. The creators, the Duffer Brothers, discovered Survive's music and used a track in an early pitch trailer. Dixon and Stein were then commissioned to write the score. Only the two of them took it on, because the production could not accommodate the whole band. Their main title theme won a Primetime Emmy Award in 2017, and the first two volumes of the soundtrack were nominated for a Grammy. The score was released on several albums, from Stranger Things 2 to Stranger Things 4. They also wrote music for the virtual reality series Spheres, the film Native Son and Meow Wolf's installation Convergence Station in Denver.

The sound refers to the synthesizer music of 1980s film and television, with pulsing arpeggios and menacing sounds, and grew along with the scale of the series. Dixon and Stein show that a modern television score made with analogue instruments can have a distinctive, recognisable sound of its own.
artiest/kyle-dixon.listen: Listen to the Stranger Things main title theme and notice the pulsing synthesizer line that begins almost like a heartbeat and slowly builds tension.

artiest/kyle-dixon-en-michael-stein.text:
Kyle Dixon and Michael Stein are two American composers and electronic musicians. They began working together in the electronic music scene of Austin, Texas. In 2009, with Adam Jones and Mark Donica, they founded the synthesizer band Survive. That band is known for analogue synthesizers, playing live with hardware and electronic compositions influenced by the music of horror and science fiction films. For film, television and other media Dixon and Stein work under the name Short Hour.

Their breakthrough came with the score for the Netflix series Stranger Things. The series' creators, the Duffer Brothers, discovered Survive's music and used a track by the band in an early promotional film for the series. Only Dixon and Stein then took on the score, because the production could not accommodate the whole band. The music was released on several soundtrack albums, starting in 2016. The main title theme won a Primetime Emmy Award in 2017, and the first two volumes received a Grammy nomination.

They have also written music outside Stranger Things, including for the virtual reality series Spheres and the film Native Son. Their work shows how the sound of analogue synthesizers from 1980s film music can work again as contemporary television music.
artiest/kyle-dixon-en-michael-stein.listen: Listen to Stranger Things and notice the pulsing synthesizer pattern with which the theme begins. Try to hear how the electronic sounds, built up layer by layer, create tension.

artiest/kylie-minogue.text:
Kylie Minogue was born in Melbourne, Australia, in 1968. She became known as Charlene Mitchell in the Australian soap Neighbours, in which she appeared from 1986 to 1988. Through the London producing trio Stock Aitken Waterman she grew into a pop star with a career of almost forty years. Worldwide she has sold more than 80 million records.

Her first single, Locomotion (1987), was released only in Australia and became the best-selling single of the decade there. She then travelled to London. SAW had forgotten that she was coming; while Minogue waited outside, they wrote I Should Be So Lucky in about forty minutes. The song, with synthesizers, orchestra hits and a LinnDrum drum machine, spent five weeks at number 1 in England and six weeks in Australia. Her debut album Kylie (1988) became the best-selling album by a woman in England in the 1980s. With her Neighbours co-star Jason Donovan she sang Especially for You, also an English number 1.

At the end of 1992 her contract with SAW's label expired. At Deconstruction she made the albums Kylie Minogue (1994) and Impossible Princess (1997). With Spinning Around (2000) and Can't Get You Out of My Head (2001) she returned to the dance floor. The latter song reached number one in more than forty countries. In 2005 she was diagnosed with breast cancer and had to cut a tour short. Minogue showed that a star from the hit factory could grow into an artist who lasts for decades. In 2023 Tension was released.
artiest/kylie-minogue.listen: I Should Be So Lucky (1987) is SAW at its simplest. Notice the thin LinnDrum drum machine, the synthesizers and the orchestra hits: short, hard blasts from a whole orchestra at once.

artiest/kyoto-nohgaku-kai.text:
Kyoto Nohgaku Kai is a company of musicians and singers from Kyoto that performs the music of Japanese Noh theatre. The album Japanese Noh Music includes excerpts from Hagoromo, one of the best-known Noh plays, about a heavenly woman who wants her feather robe back, and the instrumental pieces Jo-no-mai and Deha.

Noh is the oldest major theatre form in Japan that is still regularly performed. It arose in the fourteenth century, when the actor Kan'ami and his son Zeami combined older forms of dance, song and popular entertainment into a new, refined theatre. With the support of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, Noh became the country's most important performing art. After that it hardly changed: actors and musicians learned to imitate every movement and every sound exactly, so that over the centuries the tempo became ever slower and more solemn.

The music is made by a small ensemble, the hayashi, with four instruments: a transverse flute, the nohkan, two hourglass-shaped drums played on the shoulder and on the hip, and a drum struck with sticks. To this is added a chorus of six to eight singers. A piece follows the principle of jo-ha-kyū: it begins slowly, gradually speeds up and ends in a climax. To Western ears Noh often sounds strange, but it shows how music, text and movement form a single whole in an age-old tradition.
artiest/kyoto-nohgaku-kai.listen: Listen to Jo-no-mai and notice the sharp, high sound of the nohkan and the dry strokes of the drums. Notice also the calls of the drummers between the beats: these vocal sounds are part of the music and set the tempo.

artiest/l-african-jazz.text:
African Jazz, officially Le Grand Kallé et l'African Jazz, was one of the most influential Congolese rumba bands of the twentieth century. Joseph Athanase Tshamala Kabasele, known as Le Grand Kallé, founded the group in 1953 in Léopoldville, present-day Kinshasa. The band played an important role in modern Congolese popular music, at the end of the colonial era and in the first years after independence. The word jazz here had little to do with American music: in Belgian Congo it stood for elegance and modernity, and many other African bands adopted it.

The group combined traditional Central African instruments, such as the Tetela tam-tam, the ngongi and the lokole, with Western guitars, brass and percussion. In this way a worldly form of Congolese rumba came into being, the sound of city life in the 1950s and 1960s. Early hits were Parafifi and Nzela mosika, in which the guitarist Nico Kasanda stood out. Later members included Vicky Longomba and Tabu Ley Rochereau.

In 1960 African Jazz went to the Belgian-Congolese Round Table Conference in Brussels, where Kabasele had to put together an orchestra for the delegation. Indépendance Cha Cha, recorded there, became an African independence anthem. The band then toured Belgium, the Netherlands and France. From 1963 important members, including Tabu Ley Rochereau and Nico Kasanda, left to start African Fiesta, and the original line-up fell apart.
artiest/l-african-jazz.listen: Listen to Indépendance Cha Cha and notice the light, danceable cha-cha-cha rhythms and the guitar lines that, together with the singing, give voice to the celebration of independence.

artiest/l-itineraire.text:
Ensemble l'Itinéraire is a French contemporary music ensemble based in Paris and one of the most important in Europe. It was founded in January 1973 by the composers Michaël Lévinas, Tristan Murail, Hugues Dufourt, Gérard Grisey and Roger Tessier. Lévinas is the son of the philosopher Emmanuel Levinas. Many of the composers had studied at IRCAM.

The ensemble is best known for performing spectral music. Spectral music changes tone colour by composing orchestral masses: the composer builds the sound from the properties of sound itself, rather than from melodies and chords. Since its foundation l'Itinéraire has worked with many composers and has brought hundreds of new works into being.

This search can be heard on the recordings. Saturne from 1980 is one of the early recordings, La conférence des oiseaux appeared in 1999, and there are records with work by Marc-André Dalbavie and Charleston from 2008. The ensemble showed how a small group of musicians could open up new sound worlds. Anyone who wants to follow the development of contemporary music since the 1970s will come across l'Itinéraire as one of the first groups to give spectral music a permanent place in concert life.
artiest/l-itineraire.listen: Listen to a recording by the ensemble, for example from Saturne, and notice how the sound changes slowly and how the colour of the instruments matters more than a melody.

artiest/l-subramaniam.text:
Lakshminarayana Subramaniam is an Indian violinist, composer and conductor, born in Madras in 1947. He grew up in Jaffna, had lessons from the age of five from his father, the violinist V. Lakshminarayana, and gave his first concert at the age of six. He studied medicine in Madras and worked as a general practitioner, but then chose music. Later he took a master's degree in Western classical music at the California Institute of the Arts. He is thus trained both in Carnatic music and in the Western tradition.

Since 1973 he has made more than two hundred recordings. He has played with Yehudi Menuhin, Stéphane Grappelli, Jean-Luc Ponty, Herbie Hancock, Stanley Clarke and George Harrison, and in the late 1970s with Ali Akbar Khan, in one of the first jugalbandis between South Indian and Hindustani musicians. His records of the 1980s include Indian Express, Spanish Wave, Conversations and Fantasy Without Limits. In 1983 he wrote a Double Concerto for violin and flute, in which Western scales and microtones come together, and in 1985 Fantasy on Vedic Chants, which was premiered with the New York Philharmonic.

Subramaniam has also written for orchestras, ballet and Hollywood films and has published books about music. He performs with his daughter Bindu, his son Ambi and his wife, the singer Kavita Krishnamurthy. He showed that the South Indian violin can have a permanent place in jazz, classical music and world music.
artiest/l-subramaniam.listen: Listen to a recording of Fantasy Without Limits or Indian Express and notice the long, gliding tone of the violin, which in Carnatic music imitates the human voice.

artiest/la-la-land-cast.text:
La La Land is an American musical film from 2016, written and directed by Damien Chazelle. Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone play a jazz pianist and an aspiring actress who fall in love while pursuing their dreams in Los Angeles. The cast sing the songs themselves. The music was composed by Justin Hurwitz, who wrote the songs with the lyricists Benj Pasek and Justin Paul. Chazelle and Hurwitz had come up with the idea as students at Harvard.

The film opens with Another Day of Sun, a number that begins in a traffic jam in Los Angeles. Among the other songs we hear Someone in the Crowd, A Lovely Night, City of Stars and Audition (The Fools Who Dream). Chazelle drew inspiration from the French films of Jacques Demy, such as The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, and from classic Hollywood musicals such as Singin' in the Rain and An American in Paris. Jazz plays a large part in the story.

Many studios did not want to finance an original, contemporary jazz musical. After the success of Whiplash it did become possible. La La Land received fourteen Oscar nominations, a record that has been equalled, and won six Oscars, including best director and best actress. In doing so the film brought the musical back to a large audience.
artiest/la-la-land-cast.listen: Listen to Another Day of Sun and notice how an ordinary traffic moment turns into a big song-and-dance number with many voices. Which rhythms and instruments do you hear coming back?

artiest/la-magnifica-comunita.text:
La Magnifica Comunità is an Italian ensemble for Baroque music and classical chamber music. Its recordings show what it is known for: the work of Luigi Boccherini. The group recorded all the string quintets in a multi-volume series, including opuses 11, 13, 18 and 20, and also the complete guitar quintets. Records with Antonio Vivaldi, the violin concertos Op. 8 including Le Quattro Stagioni, and with a Christmas cantata by Alessandro Stradella have also appeared.

Boccherini himself was born in Lucca in 1743 and was a cellist and composer of the Classical period. He worked in Madrid under a Spanish patron, the Infante Luis Antonio, and wrote much of his best-known work there. His chamber music often follows the model of Joseph Haydn, but gives the cello a larger role. The minuet from the String Quintet in E, Op. 11 No. 5, is his best-known piece. The finale of the fourth guitar quintet is a fandango, a lively Spanish dance.

By recording this music in a fixed series, La Magnifica Comunità brings to the fore a composer who long stood in the shadow of Haydn and Mozart. The ensemble plays an elegant, galant music with plenty of dance and song. Anyone who wants to hear Boccherini and Vivaldi as they were meant to be heard, in a small line-up with clear lines, will find a good way in here.
artiest/la-magnifica-comunita.listen: Listen to the minuet from Boccherini's String Quintet in E, Op. 11 No. 5, and notice the graceful melody in the first violin, accompanied by a gently dancing cello.

artiest/la-monte-young.text:
La Monte Young is an American composer and musician, born in 1935 in a log cabin in Bern, Idaho. As a child he was fascinated by sustained sounds: the wind along the house and the humming of transformers on the telephone poles. In Los Angeles he played jazz saxophone, with Ornette Coleman and Eric Dolphy among others, and studied composition. He was influenced by Anton Webern, Gregorian chant, Indian classical music, Japanese gagaku and Indonesian gamelan. In 1959 he attended the summer course in Darmstadt with Karlheinz Stockhausen and became acquainted with the work of John Cage.

His Trio for Strings from 1958, with long sustained tones, is sometimes called the starting point of minimal music. In 1960 he moved to New York, where he became a central figure in the Fluxus movement. His Compositions 1960 were short text scores: one of them consists of two notes with the instruction that they be held for a long time. With his wife, the light artist Marian Zazeela, he founded the Theatre of Eternal Music, in which Tony Conrad and John Cale also played. They made music of droning, endless tones. With Zazeela he also built Dream House, a space full of sound and light where the music sounds continuously. From 1970 he studied Indian singing with Pandit Pran Nath.

Young released few records, but his influence is great. Through John Cale his long, sustained tones found their way into the music of The Velvet Underground, and his work is seen as a source for drone music and ambient.
artiest/la-monte-young.listen: Listen to an excerpt of Inside the Dream Syndicate, Volume I: Day of Niagara, recorded in 1965 with John Cale and Tony Conrad among others. Notice how the strings and voices keep holding the same tones, and how after a while you begin to hear small vibrations and overtones in what at first seemed one monotonous sound.

artiest/la-nina-de-los-peines.text:
Pastora Pavón Cruz, known as La Niña de los Peines, was born in Seville in 1890 and died in 1969. She is regarded as the most important female flamenco singer of the twentieth century. She came from a family of singers: her brother Tomás Pavón was also an important singer. At the age of eight she sang in public for the first time, at the spring fair in Seville. She got her nickname, the girl of the combs, in a café in Madrid, from a tango verse about combs. She herself disliked the name.

In 1910 she made her first recordings. In 1922 she performed at the Concurso de Cante Jondo in Granada, which was organised partly by Manuel de Falla and Federico García Lorca in order to renew flamenco. Lorca admired her voice. She sang all the palos, the flamenco forms, but excelled above all in siguiriyas, soleares, tangos and bulerías. She preserved styles that were in danger of disappearing, such as the siguiriyas of Ciego de la Peña and El Marruro. She never learned to read or write.

The singing of La Niña de los Peines is rough, powerful and expressive, with tones between the notes of the Western scale. For later singers such as Antonio Mairena she was an example. In this way she forms a link between the traditional flamenco of the nineteenth century and the revival of the old forms in the 1950s to 1970s.
artiest/la-nina-de-los-peines.listen: Listen to De dos vereas inguales (soleares) and notice how the voice stretches and bends the melody. Do you hear the long, raw outbursts and how little there is beneath the voice?

artiest/labi-siffre.text:
Labi Siffre, whose full name is Claudius Afolabi Siffre, is a British singer, songwriter and poet, born in London in 1945. His father was a Yoruba from Nigeria, his mother had Barbadian roots. As a child, on hearing One for My Baby by Frank Sinatra, he became convinced that music would be important to him. He studied at the Eric Gilder School of Music in Soho, worked as a taxi driver and a delivery man and in the 1960s played jazz guitar in Annie Ross's club.

In 1970 he signed with Pye International and his first album came out, including a cover of Words by the Bee Gees. Success failed to come. His second album, The Singer and the Song, contained only his own work. In 1972 two hits followed from the album Crying Laughing Loving Lying: the title song and It Must Be Love, later covered by Madness. His best-known song came in 1987, (Something Inside) So Strong. He wrote it after a television documentary and directed it against apartheid. The song reached number four in Britain and earned him an Ivor Novello Award.

Siffre also wrote essays, a stage and television play and three volumes of poetry. His music is personal and direct: an acoustic guitar, a warm voice and lyrics in which love and social indignation stand side by side. He showed that a pop song can carry a political message without losing its melody.
artiest/labi-siffre.listen: Listen to (Something Inside) So Strong and notice how the vocal line slowly builds and how the lyrics about dignity and resistance grow ever more powerful.

artiest/lady-gaga.text:
Lady Gaga's real name is Stefani Germanotta. She was born in New York in 1986 and had piano lessons from the age of four. As a teenager she played at open mic nights and in school theatre. She briefly studied at the arts programme of New York University, but dropped out to concentrate on music. In the clubs of the Lower East Side she performed with her own band and in burlesque shows with the performance artist Lady Starlight. Her stage name is derived from the Queen song Radio Ga Ga.

Her debut album The Fame, made with the producer RedOne, was released in 2008. The singles Just Dance and Poker Face reached number 1 in many countries, and Poker Face was the best-selling single of 2009. The Fame Monster (2009) included Bad Romance, Telephone with Beyoncé and Alejandro. Born This Way (2011), Artpop (2013), a jazz album with Tony Bennett, Cheek to Cheek (2014), and the soft rock album Joanne (2016) followed. For the film A Star Is Born (2018) she sang Shallow. Later she returned to danceable pop with Chromatica (2020) and Mayhem (2025).

Gaga combines electronic dance pop with the glam rock of David Bowie and Queen. Just as important is her image: she founded the creative team Haus of Gaga, on the model of Andy Warhol's Factory, and constantly changes her look, costume and style. In this she follows the model that Madonna, Michael Jackson and Prince set out in the 1980s: a pop star as a total work of art made of music, video, fashion and show.
artiest/lady-gaga.listen: Listen to Bad Romance and notice the opening: Gaga sings a short series of sounds without real words, rah-rah-ah-ah-ah, which keeps returning later. Hear how the chorus then comes in with a heavy synthesizer bass and a pounding beat.

artiest/ladysmith-black-mambazo.text:
Ladysmith Black Mambazo is a South African male choir that sings in the styles of isicathamiya and mbube. Joseph Shabalala founded the first version in 1960, under the name Ezimnyama, with brothers and cousins who had grown up together on the farm. In 1964 he had dreams for half a year about a choir singing in perfect harmony, and he tried to teach his group that sound. The name combines Ladysmith, the family's home town, the black ox as the strongest animal on the farm, and mambazo, the Zulu word for axe. The choir won so often that in the early 1970s it was no longer allowed to take part in the competitions.

In 1972 the group signed a contract with Gallo. The album Amabutho appeared in 1973. After Shabalala's conversion to Christianity in 1976 many religious songs were added, and Ukukhanya Kwelanga became a success. The choir became known worldwide with Paul Simon's 1986 album Graceland. Simon then produced the album Shaka Zulu, which won a Grammy in 1988.

The music is polyphonic singing without instruments, with deep basses as the foundation and a lead singer above them. In this way the choir brought the South African singing tradition to an international audience. Nelson Mandela called the members South Africa's cultural ambassadors.
artiest/ladysmith-black-mambazo.listen: Listen to Nomathemba and notice how the deep bass voices form the foundation while the higher voices answer above them. Try to hear where the lead singer guides the sound of the choir.

artiest/ladytron.text:
Ladytron is a British electronic band formed in Liverpool in 1999. The producers and DJs Daniel Hunt and Reuben Wu took the name from the Roxy Music song Ladytron. In the summer of 1999 the Scottish Helen Marnie and the Bulgarian-Israeli Mira Aroyo joined as singers and keyboard players. Wu left the band in 2023. Some songs contain lyrics by Aroyo in her native Bulgarian.

The debut album 604 appeared in 2001. The second album, Light & Magic from 2002, sounded darker and contains Seventeen, Blue Jeans and Evil. Witching Hour was released in 2005 and contains Destroy Everything You Touch, the band's best-known song. Velocifero followed in 2008 and Gravity the Seducer in 2011, among others. In all they have made eight studio albums. In the early years the members wore uniforms, inspired by the film The Andromeda Strain.

The group calls its sound electronic pop. Critics speak of synth-pop and electronic rock. The singing is cool and often whispered, with many synthesizers. In 2009 Brian Eno called Ladytron the best of English pop music. It shows how the electronic pop of the 1980s was given new life in the twenty-first century.
artiest/ladytron.listen: Listen to Seventeen and notice how the synthesizers lay down a cold, tight rhythm while the singing remains almost unmoved. What mood does that contrast create?

artiest/laidback-luke.text:
Laidback Luke is the pseudonym of Lucas van Scheppingen, born in 1976 in Manila to a Dutch father and a Filipino mother. He grew up in Hoofddorp. As a teenager he was introduced to club music at a school party, learned to sample with an Amiga computer and bought a synthesizer. His models were Chicago house and the hard techno from Europe. The Dutch DJ Dobre helped him to his first record deal when he was eighteen.

In the mid-1990s he began releasing records under the name Laidback Luke. His first album Psyched Up appeared in 1998, followed by Electronic Satisfaction in 2002 and the mix album Windmill Skill in 2003. That year he also remixed Crescendolls by Daft Punk. At the end of the 2000s he became a central figure in electro house, collaborating with Steve Angello, Sebastian Ingrosso and Axwell, the later Swedish House Mafia. His version of Robin S.'s Show Me Love, made together with Angello, reached number eleven in the British chart in 2009. He also founded the label Mixmash Records.

His sound is hard and danceable, with heavy bass lines and plenty of energy, a mix of indie taste and floor-shaking electronic music. Laidback Luke is regarded as one of the key figures in the rise of electro house and Dutch house, and as a DJ who also gave other producers a platform.
artiest/laidback-luke.listen: Listen to his version of Show Me Love and notice how Robin S.'s familiar vocal line lands on a hard, driving electronic rhythm section.

artiest/lalah-hathaway.text:
Lalah Hathaway, born in Chicago in 1968, is an American singer, songwriter and producer. She is the eldest daughter of the soul singer Donny Hathaway and was therefore called the First Daughter of Soul. Her father died when she was ten. Her mother was a classically trained singer. Lalah learned piano at the American Conservatory of Music, wrote her first songs at the Chicago Academy for the Arts and later went to Berklee College of Music.

Her first album, Lalah Hathaway, appeared in 1990, with the single Heaven Knows. The follow-up A Moment from 1994 failed to catch on, and Virgin Records let her go. In 1999 The Song Lives On appeared, a collaboration with Joe Sample, and in 2004 Outrun the Sky with Forever, for Always, for Love. Self Portrait from 2008 and Where It All Begins on Stax Records followed. In 2014 she won a Grammy for Something, which she sang on Snarky Puppy's Family Dinner Volume 1, and in 2015 a Grammy for Jesus Children followed. Her live record from 2015 earned three Grammys, including that for best R&B album. In 2017 and 2024 she released Honestly and Vantablack on her own label.

Her voice is warm and agile, with a large range, and her music moves between soul, R&B and jazz. She stands in the line of her father, but has a sound of her own, and works a great deal with jazz musicians. In 2022 she received an honorary doctorate from Berklee.
artiest/lalah-hathaway.listen: Listen to Something with Snarky Puppy and notice how her voice switches between soft, almost whispered passages and full outbursts, while the band follows her precisely.

artiest/lalgudi-jayaraman.text:
Lalgudi Gopal Jayaraman was born in 1930 and died in 2013. He was an Indian violinist, singer and composer in Carnatic music, the classical music of South India. Together with M.S. Gopalakrishnan and T.N. Krishnan he was counted among the violin trio of Carnatic music. His father taught him the tradition, which goes back through four generations to the composer Tyagaraja. At the age of twelve he began as an accompanist to singers, before becoming a celebrated soloist.

Jayaraman developed his own way of playing the violin, known as the Lalgudi Bani. He brought the style of the human voice to the violin. He wrote kritis, tillanas and varnams, compositions that connect melody, rhythm and text and are popular with Bharatanatyam dancers. In 1966 he introduced an ensemble of violin, flute and veena. He was also the first to bring the Carnatic violin to international attention. Yehudi Menuhin was so impressed after the Edinburgh Festival of 1965 that he gave him his Italian violin.

For his work he received, among other honours, the Padma Shri in 1972 and the Padma Bhushan in 2001. His children and pupils continue his work. His influence lies in a violinist who put Indian classical music on the world map both as a soloist and as an accompanist.
artiest/lalgudi-jayaraman.listen: Listen to Jagadananda Karaka and notice how the violin follows and ornaments the vocal melody. Do you hear the flowing glides between the notes?

artiest/lalo-schifrin.text: Lalo Schifrin, from Buenos Aires, studied classical music, including in Paris, and played jazz piano. In the US he became Dizzy Gillespie's pianist and arranger. From the mid-1960s he worked in Hollywood. His theme for the TV series Mission: Impossible (1966) is in an unusual 5/4 time. It became one of the best-known TV themes. In films such as Cool Hand Luke (1967), Bullitt (1968) and Dirty Harry (1971) he mixed jazz, funk, Latin and orchestra. In this way the sound of the American police film came into being. For Enter the Dragon (1973) he added Asian sounds to funk rhythms.
artiest/lalo-schifrin.listen: Notice the unusual time signature of Mission: Impossible and the funk bass, flute and brass stabs in Bullitt.

artiest/lambert-hendricks-en-ross.text:
Lambert, Hendricks & Ross was an American jazz vocal trio, formed in 1957 by the singers Dave Lambert, Jon Hendricks and Annie Ross. Lambert had already sung with Gene Krupa in the 1940s and with groups of his own, Hendricks wrote most of the lyrics, and Ross had earlier sung jazz solos in the style of vocalese. In vocalese an existing instrumental piece or solo is given words, which the singers then sing exactly to the music.

The debut album Sing a Song of Basie appeared in 1958 on ABC-Paramount and contains songs from Count Basie's repertoire. It was so successful that the Count Basie Orchestra took part in Sing Along with Basie. From 1959 the trio recorded three albums for Columbia, including Sing Ellington, and in 1962 High Flying won a Grammy. Readers of DownBeat voted the group best vocal group from 1959 to 1963. In 1962 Ross left the trio and Yolande Bavan took her place. In 1964 the group broke up.

The three sing at breakneck speed, tightly attuned to one another, as if they were the brass section of a big band. Lambert died in 1966 in a traffic accident, which made a reunion impossible. The trio's influence is great on later jazz singers, such as The Manhattan Transfer, Al Jarreau and Bobby McFerrin.
artiest/lambert-hendricks-en-ross.listen: Listen to Cloudburst and notice how fast the voices sing the words together. Try to hear which voice carries the melody and which support the others in the background.

artiest/lamberto-gardelli.text:
Lamberto Gardelli was an Italian conductor who later became a Swedish citizen. He was born in Venice in 1915 and studied in Pesaro and at the Accademia Nazionale di Santa Cecilia in Rome. He began as a pianist and double bass player, also took composition lessons with Goffredo Petrassi and was assistant to Tullio Serafin for eight years. In 1944 he made his debut as a conductor with La traviata in Rome. He himself wrote five operas, of which only L'impresario delle Americhe was performed, and a post-Romantic Requiem.

In Stockholm Gardelli worked at the Royal Opera with singers such as Jussi Björling and Birgit Nilsson, and he was later a conductor in Copenhagen, music director of the Hungarian State Opera in Budapest and chief conductor in Munich and of the Danish Radio Symphony Orchestra. He also conducted at Glyndebourne, in London and, in 1966, for the first time at the Metropolitan Opera in New York.

He was regarded as a Verdi specialist. In the 1960s and 1970s he recorded forgotten early Verdi operas for Philips and Orfeo, such as Alzira, Attila, Stiffelio and I masnadieri, alongside Nabucco and Macbeth. He also made the first complete French version of Rossini's Guillaume Tell and recorded four operas by Respighi. He coached young sopranos, including Sylvia Sass and Lucia Aliberti. One critic praised his grasp of structure and his tasteful expression without exaggeration.
artiest/lamberto-gardelli.listen: Listen to his recording of Nabucco and notice the chorus in the famous choral scene and how the orchestra lets the singing breathe without letting the tempo sag.

artiest/lamont-dozier.text:
Lamont Dozier was an American songwriter, producer and singer from Detroit. He was born in 1941 and as a young singer recorded a few records for small labels in his city, without success. In 1962 Berry Gordy brought him to Motown. There he began working with the brothers Brian and Eddie Holland, and he put his singing career on hold. The trio became known as Holland-Dozier-Holland. Dozier and Brian Holland took care of the music, the arrangements and the production, Eddie Holland mainly of the lyrics and the vocals.

The team first scored in 1963 with Martha and the Vandellas, including Heat Wave and Quicksand. A year later, with Where Did Our Love Go, a long run of number 1 hits for The Supremes began, followed by Stop! In the Name of Love, among others. The Four Tops, The Marvelettes, Marvin Gaye and the Isley Brothers also sang their songs. Dozier named I Hear a Symphony and My World Is Empty Without You as his favourites. The trio's songs, with their driving rhythms and singalong choruses, largely defined the Motown sound.

After a quarrel with Gordy over contract and rights, the trio left Motown at the end of the 1960s and started their own labels, Invictus and Hot Wax. Dozier began singing for himself again and in 1974 had his biggest solo hit with Trying to Hold on to My Woman. Later he wrote Two Hearts for the film Buster (1988) with Phil Collins, and worked with Mick Hucknall of Simply Red. In 1990 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the Hollands. He died in 2022.
artiest/lamont-dozier.listen: Listen to Where Did Our Love Go by The Supremes. Notice the simple, stomping rhythm beneath the vocals and how the chorus keeps coming back, so that you can sing along after hearing it just once.

artiest/lange-frans-en-baas-b.text:
Lange Frans & Baas B is a Dutch hip hop duo from Diemen. Lange Frans is the pseudonym of Frans Frederiks, Baas B that of Bart Zeilstra. In 1997, after a freestyle session on a basketball court, they started the collective D-Men, together with Frans's brother Brutus. In English the name sounds like Diemen. Their first single, Zoveel Mensen, appeared in 1999, and in 2001 they won a talent contest run by Stichting Grap. Later Brace, Yes-R and Soesi B also joined the collective.

In 2004 they released singles as a duo. Moppie became a big hit, with a chorus sung by Brace. Zinloos, a protest against senseless violence, reached number one in the Dutch chart at the end of the year. After the murder of Theo van Gogh in November 2004 they recorded a version with altered lyrics. Their albums are Supervisie from 2003, Het land van from 2005 and Verder from 2008.

The lyrics are in Dutch, with a direct, street-smart tone and a light, melodic accompaniment. The duo brought Dutch-language hip hop to a large audience, at a time when it lived mainly in the underground. Success faded after 2006, partly after an incident in which Lange Frans hit a student. In 2008 the single Kamervragen and the album Verder followed, both of which disappointed. In 2009 they announced that they would stop, with a final performance on X Factor.
artiest/lange-frans-en-baas-b.listen: Listen to Zinloos and notice the calm accompaniment beneath the fast, clear Dutch raps and the chorus sung by a female singer.

artiest/larry-carlton.text:
Larry Carlton is an American guitarist, born in Torrance, California, in 1948. He had guitar lessons at the age of six and as a schoolboy played surf guitar with Eddie and the Showmen. Jazz guitarists such as Joe Pass, Barney Kessel and Wes Montgomery, and the bluesman B.B. King, were his models. In the 1970s he grew into one of the most sought-after studio guitarists in Los Angeles. He played on hundreds of records, and on more than a hundred gold records, in pop, rock, soul, jazz and country.

He worked for artists including Steely Dan, Joni Mitchell, Linda Ronstadt, Michael Jackson, Quincy Jones and Barbra Streisand. His guitar work on Steely Dan's Kid Charlemagne from 1976 appears on a Rolling Stone list of the best guitar songs. In 1981 he played on Mike Post's Theme from Hill Street Blues, which earned two Grammys. He then had a solo career of his own and was a member of the Crusaders and later of Fourplay. He had already recorded his first solo record in 1968. In the mid-1970s he built a studio, Room 335, named after the Gibson ES-335 for which he is famous. His version of Sleepwalk reached the pop and adult contemporary charts.

In 1988 he was shot in the throat outside his studio and was temporarily paralysed in his left arm. He recovered and kept on playing. His style is supple and melodic, shaped by jazz and blues, and his work shows how a session musician could define the sound of an entire era.
artiest/larry-carlton.listen: Listen to Kid Charlemagne by Steely Dan and notice the guitar solo, in which he combines bluesy notes with a clear, almost singing tone.

artiest/larry-grenadier.text:
Larry Grenadier is an American jazz double bassist, born in San Francisco in 1966. His father played trumpet in Second World War army bands. Larry himself began on trumpet and switched to bass a year later. His older brother Phil played jazz records, and Larry listened to bassists such as Ray Brown, Charles Mingus, Paul Chambers and Wilbur Ware. At twelve he began formal lessons, and at sixteen he was already playing in the Bay Area with musicians such as Bobby Hutcherson, Joe Henderson and Eddie Henderson. At Stanford he studied English literature and got to know Stan Getz, with whom he toured.

After his studies he moved to Boston to play with the vibraphonist Gary Burton, and in 1991 to New York. There he worked with Joshua Redman, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Mark Turner, Tom Harrell, Betty Carter and, again, Joe Henderson, among others. In the early 1990s he met the pianist Brad Mehldau, and he became a member of Mehldau's trio with the drummer Jorge Rossy. They toured and recorded for more than ten years. In 2004 Jeff Ballard took Rossy's place. He also played with the guitarist Pat Metheny in a trio with the drummer Bill Stewart, which he calls a great learning experience.

Under his own name he made albums such as Fear of Roaming, Songs, Costumes Are Mandatory and Driftwood. His playing is warm and melodic, and he is above all a bassist who listens and supports the others. Through his work with Mehldau and Metheny he is counted among the important bassists of contemporary jazz.
artiest/larry-grenadier.listen: Listen to a track by Brad Mehldau's trio and notice the bass, which does not only keep the rhythm but also plays a melody of its own alongside the piano.

artiest/larry-levan.text:
Larry Levan was an American DJ from New York. He was born in Brooklyn in 1954 as Lawrence Philpot and got his love of blues, jazz and gospel from his mother. As a teenager he left school and worked as a tailor in the ballroom scene of Harlem, where he became friends with Frankie Knuckles. Through David Mancuso he got to know The Loft, a private dance party with an exceptional sound system. There his idea of music that would never stop took shape. Together with Knuckles he began as a DJ at the Continental Baths.

In 1977 Levan got a regular slot at the Paradise Garage, a members-only club in Greenwich Village. For ten years he played there on Saturday nights, and his regular crowd called those evenings the Saturday Mass. He was known for his deep, dark bass and for his idiosyncratic choice of records, from Chaka Khan and Evelyn Champagne King to Kraftwerk and British synth-pop. He brought the echoes and open spaces of dub to dance music and experimented with drum machines and synthesizers. In the 1980s he made remixes of, among others, Gwen Guthrie's Ain't Nothin' Goin On But The Rent and produced Don't Make Me Wait by his own group, the Peech Boys.

The Paradise Garage closed in 1987 with a 48-hour party. Levan became addicted and no longer found a regular place in New York, but in Europe and Japan he was still thoroughly celebrated. He died in 1992, aged 38. The Garage was regarded as the model for the modern dance club, and his name lives on in the style garage house.
artiest/larry-levan.listen: Listen to Don't Make Me Wait by the Peech Boys. Notice the gospel-like vocals, the tinkling piano and the echoes and empty spaces that come from dub.
